_help: Triage settings for the test dashboard (reports/index.html). Shared through git: edit, commit, push.
modules: the app's areas, who owns each, and areas deliberately not tested (shown as coverage gaps or exclusions).
tests: module (and severity, when the title has no [P0]-[P3] tag) per test ID. A [P0]/[P1] tag in the test title sets the severity. Default P2.

issues: per error signature: owner, ticket link, known issue. The dashboard's Assign / Ticket / Mark as known buttons edit these in your browser; 'Download triage.json' then gives you this file with your changes, to replace it here.
ticket.newIssueUrl: where 'Create ticket' opens a pre-filled issue (GitHub style ?title=&body=). Empty = the button copies the ticket text instead.
knownApi: API problems that are understood and not a test failure; matched against the call's endpoint or URL. Shown grey, not red, and never a budget warning.

knownLogLines: lines in the app's Android log that are understood and not an app problem: [{ match: 'regular expression on the log line', reason }]. They stay listed in the test's App log, but do not count as app errors or make a test 'passed with warnings'.

quarantine: tests whose failures do not count towards the verdict until a date: [{ test, reason, owner, until: 'YYYY-MM-DD', ticket, added }]. After 'until' the failure counts again and the verdict says the quarantine expired. The dashboard's Quarantine button adds entries (then Download triage.json).

categoryRules: your own rules for failure categories, checked before the built-in ones: [{ match: 'regular expression on the error message', category: 'product' | 'test' | 'environment' | 'infrastructure' | 'review', why: 'shown as the reason' }]. issues.<signature>.category overrides one failure by hand.

SESSION._why: The test session could not start: nothing was tested.

knownLogLines.match: E adservices: Failed binding to measurement service
knownLogLines.reason: Google's ad-measurement service (part of Google Play services) is not available on the emulator's Android image; a library in the app tries to reach it. Not an app problem.
React Native logs this at error level when a screen is closed or the app goes to the background. Normal.

knownLogLines.match: ReactNative: Tried to remove non-existent frame callback
knownLogLines.reason: React Native's own message when an animation frame callback is cleaned up twice, e.g. when a screen closes. Harmless.

knownLogLines.match: No package ID [0-9a-f]+ found for resource ID 0x
knownLogLines.reason: Android could not resolve a resource ID from another package (a library or WebView asking for an overlay resource). Harmless unless something on screen is missing.

knownLogLines.match: SwipeRefreshLayout: Got ACTION_MOVE event but don't have an active pointer id
knownLogLines.reason: Android's pull-to-refresh widget logs this for scroll gestures injected by the test (UiAutomator). Not seen with a real finger; not an app problem.
The emulator's graphics layer (gfxstream) answering an OpenGL query it does not support. Emulator only.

knownLogLines.match: (LegacySurfaceTexture is not attached|clearBuffersForDisconnectLocked|cancelBuffer given a leaked buffer)
knownLogLines.reason: Android's graphics surfaces being torn down when a screen with video or animation closes. Harmless; mostly seen on emulators.

knownLogLines.match: InAppUpdate: (Failed to check for update|.*Install Error\(-6\)|\s+at )
knownLogLines.reason: Google Play's in-app update check is not allowed on this device (Install Error -6: the app was not installed from Google Play, or the device state does not allow it). The app catches it and carries on. Expected on test devices; on a phone with a Play Store install it should not appear.

knownLogLines.match: IntBufferBatchMountItem: Skipping batch of MountItems; was stopped
knownLogLines.reason: React Native skipping screen updates for a screen that has already closed (same cause as the "stopping surface" lines). Harmless.

The CleverTap analytics SDK dropped one property of an analytics event because its value type is not supported (it accepts text, numbers, booleans and dates; null, lists or nested objects are dropped). Seen when Edit Profile opens (SMK-06, 18 Nov). No effect on the user; the event is still sent without that property. Developers: check the event properties sent when Edit Profile opens.

categoryRules.why: Layout checks failed: compare the screenshot with the layout spec (boxes shown on the screenshot). Either the screen changed (product) or the spec needs updating (npm run layout:accept).
